Senior Correspondent

Donald Trump struts onto the new White House helipad, an 80,000-sq.-ft. expanse of carved granite on the South Lawn. “Can you believe this?” he says, taking in the scene, the Washington Monument rising in the distance. The President lingers over the details of the project with obvious pleasure, pointing out the gray stone imported from Italy and describing how five separate sections were fitted together, with measurements he says are precise to an eighth of an inch.

U.S. President Donald Trump gestures during a press conference at a NATO summit in The Hague, Netherlands June 25, 2025. REUTERS/Yves Herman/File Photo

On Friday, a former lawyer with the Department of Justice warned that President Donald Trump is propping up “flimsy,” “politically motivated prosecutions” to bolster his claims of election fraud. This is according to former DOJ pardon attorney Liz Oyer, who writes in the New York Times that Trump’s legal attacks on a “tired mailman” and other “civilian” targets not only make a mockery of his voter fraud claims, but prove his “weakness” is growing.

“When the deputy attorney general personally announces an indictment from Justice Department headquarters, it signals a matter of national importance,” writes Oyer.
